title: T227 PNC - Why We Say 'G-d Help' When Passing Reapers
hebrewTitle: מדוע אומרים 'ה׳ יעזור' בעוברים על הקוצרים
author: Petten Nanach

beginner.en: Rebbe Nachman transmitted in the name of a tzaddik who expounded in the synagogue: when passing by reapers working in the field, the custom is to say "G-d help" or a blessing to them. This custom is rooted in deep meaning: the reapers are laboring in the physical world, and their labor has a spiritual counterpart. By blessing them, we connect physical labor to its divine source and draw down heavenly help for their work. Simple customs often carry profound spiritual architecture — every traditional practice, properly understood, is a window into higher worlds.

intermediate.en: T227: The custom of saying "Hashem ya'azor" (G-d help) when passing reapers carries deep spiritual significance — transmitted by Rebbe Nachman in the name of a tzaddik. Folk customs often encode profound spiritual connections between physical labor and its divine source. LM 227.
intermediate.he: אמירת "ה׳ יעזור" לקוצרים — מנהג בעל משמעות רוחנית עמוקה. שמע רבנו בשם צדיק. מנהגי עם פשוטים = ידיעה רוחנית עמוקה.

scholarly.he: LM א׳ רכז׳ — "שמעתי בשמו שאמר בשם צדיק אחד... מה שאומרים בעוברים על הקוצרים ה׳ יעזור".
